ai.description: *Proahaetulla antiqua* is a slender snake reaching 60 cm. It is pale brown with a dark mid-dorsal stripe and features a distinctively pointed, elongated snout and horizontal pupil.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Proahaetulla antiqua* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian vine snakes by its distinctively blunt, rounded snout, which lacks the elongated rostral appendage.
ai.habitat: *Proahaetulla antiqua* inhabits the mid-elevation evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Proahaetulla antiqua* is a diurnal snake that actively hunts for prey among forest vegetation during the day, utilizing its slender body to navigate through foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Proahaetulla antiqua* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, it is believed to reproduce seasonally during the monsoon.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Proahaetulla antiqua* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
